cells.tense: You are moving toward something and the moving itself is easy now.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Go back through something you already finished, one slow pass, hands off. No improving while you stand in it, no list of what comes next. Let the thing count as done.
cells.core:
You can go somewhere without grinding. The bends come and you follow them; feeling and direction already agree, so nothing has to be forced. What you want and where you're headed are roughly one line, and you can tell this week whether a step counted by how it sat with you. People near you may not know how much of this steadiness was chosen.

Go back through something you already finished, hands off, one slow pass, no list of what comes next. Let it count as done while you stand in it. You've been moving to the next thing without collecting the last one, and the satisfaction has to be walked into a few times before it settles. That walking is part of the work, not a pause from it.
cells.sheetLine: Movement this steady was chosen, not given.

cells.tense: If this keeps up, the destination will arrive before you can be there.
cells.act: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan
cells.ask: Set down on a page what your head knows and what your gut keeps wanting. Find the single line that holds both, then do only the part of the plan that comes off that line. Nothing past it, no new goals.
cells.core:
Somewhere in you the arrival keeps happening ahead of schedule. The goal is already won in your head, so the actual steps feel late — and you speed up, or swing to another goal that promises faster. The direction isn't wrong. The clock in you is running on a finish line nobody else has reached and nothing has crossed.

So set down on a page the two sides of the next move: the case your head makes, the pull your gut keeps making. Then write the single line that holds both and do only the part of the plan that comes off that line. That's not slowing the drive down. It's letting the drive carry only the load it can actually keep.
cells.sheetLine: The finish line arrives in your head before your feet reach it.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that closed behind you a while back.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take some stretch that finished this year and tally what it handed you — a skill, a person, a place you can walk into now. Name them and stop. No plan after, no reading them back as a lesson.
cells.core:
The motion here has stopped, and where it stopped there's little left to steer with. You still show up where you used to be pointed, but nothing in you is headed anywhere, and a few things that ended still feel open because nobody tallied them closed. You're not lazy. The direction quietly ran out while you were completing the endings, and you've been standing at a threshold that's no longer there.

Take some stretch that finished this year and tally what it handed you — a skill, a person, a place you can walk into now. Name them and stop; no plan after, no reading them back as a lesson. That's how a finished thing stops eating the fuel the next direction needs. When you can name the yield, some of the motion comes back.
cells.sheetLine: You still show up, but nothing ahead is pulling you.

cells.tense: The direction is being followed, but your name is not on it.
cells.act: keep building the thing with sustained craft
cells.ask: Add to what you're building today, and again tomorrow, same time, until it's the habit that can't be argued with. And when it comes up in conversation, give it its real size.
cells.core:
You keep the road under you from week to week and mostly don't mention it. When what you're building comes up, you say it's nothing much, or you file it under filler while the real work is somewhere else — and the direction keeps running underneath the way you describe your days, unnamed. People can see that you're going somewhere. Your own account of it has drifted a room behind.

Add to what you're building today, and again tomorrow, same time, until it's the habit that can't be argued with. And when it comes up in conversation, give it its real size. The persisting is how the direction gets taken back under your own name. Your hands are already doing it; the saying catches up last.
cells.sheetLine: You're going somewhere. Your account of it lags a room behind.
